note: Invented for a demo. Nothing here is real customer speech, and Shmuber Eats is a fictional product. Turn numbers are 1-based and match app.kb.spoken.from_speaker_text's 'turn N' locations. Each planted topic is recorded at the line that first raises it; for Control A the interviewee's answers to the follow-up elaborate that same occurrence and are not counted again. Control A lines are recorded only under their control, not under substitutions.

topics.first_order_trigger_aside: THE HIDDEN SIGNAL. The interviewee mentions, in passing, that their FIRST order was set off by a one-off situation (a sick child, a car in the garage, a house move, a work deadline, a sprained ankle, a newborn, a snowstorm, guests arriving that night), not a wish to change how they shop, and that once it passed they went back to their usual store. No hypothesis predicts it, and it undercuts the substitution bet. Never followed up: the next interviewer turn moves to a guide question.
topics.control_a_odd_swap_for_recipe: CONTROL A (followed up). The interviewee volunteers that the picker's replacement was wrong for the dish they were cooking (a coconut drink for curry coconut milk, cake flour for pizza dough, spicy tortillas for small children, margarine for buttercream, smoked salmon slices for a baked fillet). Every time, the interviewer asks a follow-up that engages it. A correct 'missed' detector must NOT flag this topic.
topics.control_b_logged_out_at_checkout: CONTROL B (below the noise floor). The app logged the interviewee out at the moment of paying. Raised in only 2 interviews, not followed up; a detector with a 3-interview floor must NOT surface it.
topics.substitutions: PROMPTED guide topic: substituted items in general (guide question s5, its follow-on questions and one pitch).
topics.delivery_window: PROMPTED guide topic: the two-hour delivery window (guide question s7 and its follow-on questions). Volunteered twice.
topics.pass_price: PROMPTED guide topic: a monthly delivery pass and its price (guide question s8, price anchors and follow-on questions).
topics.carrying_heavy_shopping: NOT PLANTED, found by the first model run (2026-11-17) and then keyed by hand: the interviewee names not having to carry heavy shopping (water, rice, bags on the bus, stairs) as a reason to order or as what they value. Always volunteered, never followed up. Two of its lines (02 t4, 07 t8) are also planted first-order asides, told as 'I could not carry it home'. Driver-courtesy remarks (01 t32, 07 t28) are not counted.

prompted_policy.prompted: An interviewee turn is PROMPTED when it answers an interviewer question or pitch about its topic, and VOLUNTEERED otherwise.
prompted_policy.pitch: A pitch or a leading question about a topic ('wouldn't it be great if we texted you before swapping anything?', 'what about 9.99 a month?') counts as asking about it.
prompted_policy.broad: A broad question asks only for what it names: 'walk me through your last order' asks HOW the order went, not WHY they ordered or what was swapped; 'how often do you order?' asks HOW OFTEN, not WHY; 'who does the shopping?' and 'how did you hear about it?' ask only that; an open question ('what did you like most?', 'what did you like least?', 'was anything confusing?', 'anything I didn't ask about?') names nothing, so what comes up in answer to it was volunteered.
prompted_policy.continuation: A follow-on question that names the topic ('did you know about the swap before the bags came?', 'would a two-hour slot work on a normal day?') asks about it, and is recorded under off_script_topic_questions.
prompted_policy.guide_s5: s5 (substitutions) counts as asked only where substitutions were asked about neutrally; a pitch about swaps is a pitch, recorded under pitches.
